name: Sea of Fortune
size: Medium-large, islands on both flanks around a central strait
description: Somewhere between France and Great Britain, with islands stacked onto both flanks and a strait cutting through the middle. The right side sits close enough for a stand-up brawl, the left stays open enough to snipe from range.

keyAreas.name: Right flank capture point
keyAreas.notes: Taller islands and tighter spacing favor cruisers and battleships willing to close the distance. Fights here open shorter than anywhere else on the map.

keyAreas.name: Left flank capture point
keyAreas.notes: The islands run low here, blocking torpedoes more than they block gunfire. Better ground for a long-range duel than a torpedo ambush.

keyAreas.name: Center strait
keyAreas.notes: A narrow passage splits the map, with a small island and its castle marking the middle. Whoever holds it controls how fast either side can reinforce the other flank.

strategyNotes: Commit to the right flank as a group. The tighter quarters punish whoever hesitates more than whoever pushes first.
Use the left flank's low islands for cover from shells, not concealment. Cruisers and battleships can still trade at range without full exposure.
Holding the center strait early makes it much harder for the enemy to shift ships between flanks once one side starts losing.
Lower-tier matches run a smaller version of this map, so flank distances shrink and the center strait matters even sooner.
